subject: KPI ops retro: June dashboard anomalies & actions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KPI ops retro: June dashboard anomalies & actions

Team —

Thanks for joining the quick post-QBR retro thread. I reviewed the June ops dashboard this morning and flagged three anomalies we need short-term mitigations for and owners for follow-up work into next week. TL;DR: p95 latency spike on 6/12-6/14, cost-per-1M tokens up 18% MoM (primarily in Hosted API), and an uptime blip during the Europe rolling deploy (2h partial degrad).

Initial asks:
- Marcus: can you validate the p95 spike attribution (model variants, routing fallbacks)? I suspect a change to continuous batching parameters but need confirmation.
- Aditya: please run a quick cost delta breakdown by route/model and whether cache hit-rate regressed.
- Laura: I want a concise note for the exec QBR appendix (one slide) — root causes & immediate mitigations, with estimates for cost savings from short-term changes.
- Jonas: log-level traces for the 6/14 incident and tracer IDs for impacted requests; aim to surface a probable rollback window.

Attachments: June-dashboard-snapshot.png (high-level visuals), kpi-variance-table.csv (metric deltas).

Plan: get owners' updates by EOD Monday 6/28 so I can fold into the leadership summary for the Wednesday leadership sync.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI ops retro: June dashboard anomalies & actions

Hannah — quick update on p95 latency: initial tracing shows a 40% increase in average batch sizes for the hosted text-generation route between 06/12 02:30 UTC and 06/14 05:00 UTC. Two things likely contributed:
1) A config rollout (continuous-batching window tuning) that unintentionally widened the batch aggregation time at peak. Change authored by platform-configs service (PR #487).
2) Cache TTL regression: prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~12% for `chat-complete-v2` around the same window (see attached kpi-variance-table.csv).

Action items I own:
- Revert the batching window change (safe) — scheduled immediate rollback to previous config by 06/27 03:00 UTC.
- Start a 48-hour canary with the old settings and monitor p95; will post results to the dashboard.

I'll push a short changelog and postmortem stub to the HC-2345 Confluence page.

-Marcus
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI ops retro: June dashboard anomalies & actions

Hannah / Marcus — I ran a cost delta and cache analysis this morning. Findings summary:
- Cost: hosted API token spend rose 18% MoM. ~60% of that is from higher token counts per request on the enterprise routes (Acme Analytics traffic surge). The remainder ~40% is from a small set of long-tail queries that iteratively call the model (chat back-and-forth).
- Cache: global prefix cache hit-rate fell from 76% to 64% during the period. The most impacted model is `chat-complete-v2` (see attached CSV).

Short-term fixes I recommend:
- Increase prefix cache TTL for non-sensitive routes from 30s to 90s for a 72-hour pilot (expect ~6-8% cost savings if hit-rate returns).
- Rate-limit a small percentage (2%) of enterprise burst traffic with protection policy while we engage Acme for best-practice usage patterns.

I'll prepare a cost impact table for Laura's slide and coordinate with Growth to loop in Acme.

- Aditya
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI ops retro: June dashboard anomalies & actions

Team — draft slide attached (retro-notes.docx). I distilled the issues into three bullets with one-line mitigations and expected delta by EOW if all short-term actions complete:
- Latency (p95): revert batching window + canary -> target return to baseline within 24-48h.
- Cost: TTL pilot + 2% burst protection -> estimated -9% token cost in Hosted API.
- Uptime: Europe rolling deploy introduced a race on node draining; Jonas to propose a safer drain window.

I also included a recommended customer-facing note (one paragraph) we can send to Acme to explain temporary rate-limiting and offer help. Approve edits and I'll finalize for the Wednesday leadership packet.

-Laura
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 13:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI ops retro: June dashboard anomalies & actions

Hannah / Laura — added initial trace snippets to HC-2345 and a recommended change to the drain script. Short summary: the Europe rolling deploy used a 60s graceful drain which, under certain traffic patterns and sticky routing, left a small percentage of requests routed to partially drained nodes. Proposed mitigation: extend drain to 180s and gate drain starts with active-request threshold.

I'll join the postmortem sync tomorrow and bring concrete tracer IDs.

-Jonas
